articles.title: Vice-President JD Vance says Republicans lost big because of war in Iran
articles.summary: President Donald Trump earlier acknowledged the Iran war was a factor but stood defiant on his decision to launch the attacks.
articles.body:
US Vice-President JD Vance has blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party's devastating losses in the midterm elections.

"The reason we lost is the war," he wrote in a lengthy post on X on Wednesday morning. "The president himself said so last night."

Vance was commenting for the first time since his party's resounding defeat - President Donald Trump earlier acknowledged the Iran war was a factor but stood defiant on his decision to launch the attacks.

Oil prices slumped below $100 (£74) a barrel to the lowest level in more than two months in response to the vice-president's comments.

Vance has long questioned US intervention abroad, and experts say with this statement he has sought to publicly distance himself from the deeply unpopular conflict ahead of a potential 2028 presidential run.

He said he had discussed Republicans' loss of Congress with pollsters who told him that it was not that Republicans failed to show up.

"The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026," Vance said.

The vice-president said the voters were angry with the administration over the Iran war, cost of living and inflation, and the current US relationship with Israel, which receives billions of dollars in annual US aid.

Elaborating further on the frustration over the war with Iran, he said: "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest."

"But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

He urged Republicans to take their anger and "get back to the work of saving our country".

"There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is," he said. "One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn't sharp enough down the stretch. I'm sure that's true."

Global oil benchmark Brent crude fell by more than 8% to about $95 a barrel on Wednesday afternoon in reaction to Vance's comments and West Texas Intermediate also fell by more than 8% to about $88 - both reaching their lowest levels in more than two months.

Despite the sharp decline, Brent remains almost 50% higher than a year ago.

Vance's comments also prompted investors to reassess the risk of a wider Middle East conflict, while markets interpreted the post-election political landscape as reducing the likelihood of a significant escalation involving Iran.

Speaking on Wednesday, President Trump said Vance's statement was "largely true", but added the conflict was necessary.

"I can tell you that as far as that war is concerned, I would have done nothing different," the president said.

Earlier, speaking to Fox News after Tuesday's election results came in, Trump said: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran, but they really probably weren't willing to do the short-term consequence of paying more for gasoline."

He also claimed Republicans "would have won easily if I was on the ballot".

The Iran war has constrained global oil supplies, which in turn have sent the price of fuel in the US to record highs - one of several economic factors that drove voters to the polls this November.

Prices increased by 3.7% in the year to September, driven higher by fuel and energy prices.

In the exit polls, nearly 80% of voters said inflation had caused them hardships - with 60% of people blaming Trump's policies for the rising cost of living.

articles.title: Bowen: Trump's loss limits powers at home, but it will likely be different abroad
articles.summary: After bruising midterm results, President Trump will want to show he can still shake the world, the BBC's international editor writes.
articles.body:
Donald Trump deals in superlatives, so there is political karma in the sheer size of the defeat handed to him by a big majority of the voters of America.

But do not expect him to go gentle into the political twilight of his career. Losing both houses of the US Congress limits his capacity to dictate, manoeuvre and disrupt at home.

As president of the United States and commander-in-chief of its armed forces he retains broad powers to use America's military might.

It is not easy to predict the actions and oscillations of Donald Trump. As president, he has turned policy u-turns into weapons. Some things, though, are constants.

One is his contempt for those he regards as losers, and his determination never to be seen as one.

The president might be tempted to blot out the electoral rout of the midterms by taking actions abroad. He might try to make moves that he can boast about as the decisive and victorious moves of a strong president, undiminished by an election that he insists, despite all the evidence, that was only lost because he was not on the ballot paper.

LIVE UPDATES: All the latest developments

In the weeks leading up to the midterms the deployment of US forces and Trump's own, often belligerent, statements ramped up talk that the US was getting ready to go back to war with Iran.

On the eve of the elections, the US carried out a limited bombing raid on an Iranian island in the Gulf.

Before he was hospitalised with a stroke, the US Senator Chris Murphy, a Democrat, went to a classified briefing about potential military options for renewed war with Iran.

Without going into detail, he condemned the plans as "insane", warning that they would trigger a "devastating escalation".

There has been speculation that the Americans have plans to bomb civilian infrastructure.

Not only would that be likely to constitute a war crime, it might also be answered by devastating Iranian strikes on equivalent targets on US allies in the Gulf. Its list of potential targets could start with the United Arab Emirates, which is as close to Israel as it is to the US.

The regime in Tehran watches political developments in the US closely . It has not concealed its satisfaction that the consequences of its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz have become a domestic political issue in the US.

Tehran is aware of the damage caused to Trump and the Republicans by the sustained rise in the prices of everything (from petrol and diesel to agricultural fertilisers) caused by the war and its attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Speaker of Iran's parliament, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, posted a warning on social media.

He said: "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message. If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare."

Benjamin Netanyahu, now acting prime minister of Israel after its election last week, and manoeuvring hard to form a new government, has repeated that he wants to bring down the Islamic regime in Tehran.

Reports in Israel and the US say that he is pushing Trump to go back to war.

Netanyahu does not have the seats to form a new government with his outgoing coalition.

But if a major war restarted and was sustained, and if Israelis came under direct fire, he could have new options of forming a unity government that he would use his considerable political skills to dominate.

The other major conflict to which Trump might turn his attention is between Ukraine and Russia, which has now lasted longer than the First World War.

Before the elections he dropped sanctions against Moscow to buy Russian diesel . He might decide to prolong and deepen sanctions relief in the hope of somehow easing the economic pressure on American consumers.

He has not been noticeably concerned about the deadly pressures on Ukrainian civilians who have been targeted by Russian ballistic missiles, now getting through in greater numbers because Ukraine's appeals for more US-made interceptors, funded by European allies, have not been answered in the way Ukraine needs and wants.

The Kremlin spokesman said Russia hoped that the election results would not impact what it called Trump's "peace-making efforts".

Donald Trump has consistently tried to force Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky into making territorial concessions to Russia to produce an agreement that would amount to capitulation for Kyiv.

Trump would add it to his improbable list of wars solved and stopped.

Smarting from electoral defeat, Trump might attempt to redouble pressure on Zelensky to accept the concessions that he has repeatedly rejected.

It is safe to say Donald Trump will continue building monuments to himself in Washington DC.

Beyond that, it is worth repeating that predictions of his next moves at home and abroad risk being wrong. But it is certain that he is not going to sit in a presidential rocking-chair and wait out his time in the White House.

Throughout his time as president, Donald Trump has relished his power and been determined to use it. That is not going to change, and there is every chance that he wants to show that if he can no longer shake America, he can shake the world.

articles.title: Armed security guard hailed as hero after fatally shooting gunman at massive Tampa Citibank site
articles.summary: Florida authorities on Wednesday confirmed a suspect and one victim are dead following a reported active shooter situation at a Tampa-area business park.
articles.body: An armed security guard was hailed as a hero by authorities Wednesday after engaging a gunman who drove onto the busy Citibank Center property in Tampa, Florida, fatally shot a woman, and then opened fire inside the building's cafeteria. The suspect crashed into an outdoor seating area where multiple people were eating lunch just after 12 p.m. upon driving through a fence at the Sabal Park Office Development, Frank Losat, a chief deputy with the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office, told reporters at the scene. The gunman then got out of his vehicle with a rifle and fatally shot a woman. An armed security guard employed by Citibank shot the suspect inside a nearby building's cafeteria during a gunfire exchange, authorities said. The gunman was taken to Tampa General Hospital where he later died. "The security guard that's employed by Citibank stopped the threat," Losat said. "Was there a potential for further violence? Absolutely. So kudos to that security guard and the people they employ." Four people were also treated at a local hospital for injuries that were not life-threatening. It is unclear where the victims were wounded during the incident. SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY CLASSIC IN ALABAMA LEAVES 1 DEAD, 8 INJURED Officials said deputies with the sheriff's office responded to the scene within minutes of the reported shooting. At the time the chaotic scene broke out, there were 3,200 Citibank employees on the property, Losat said. Another 367 law enforcement personnel responded to the scene. "With that being said, with that many witnesses… we will be doing interviews well into the night," Losat said. "The crime scene is very large. Remember, we have an outdoor scene. We have an indoor scene. Our crime scene will be processing the scene, which will take several hours, if not until tomorrow." Losat did not release the name of the suspected gunman or the victim, pending notification to the next of kin. Investigators are still trying to determine a motive for the attack. Authorities have cleared the Citibank property. FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING LEAVES 12 INJURED, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, NEAR FOOTBALL STADIUM Nearby Hillsborough College encouraged students and staff to shelter in place at the time of the incident. The FBI and ATF have also responded. The scene showed adults with children moving away from the business campus, which has a daycare center, affiliate FOX 13 Tampa Bay reported. "We are aware of an incident impacting our site in Tampa, Florida and are coordinating with law enforcement," Citibank said in a statement to Fox News Digital. Citibank employees were asked to meet at the triage area in the parking lot of the Sheraton Tampa Brandon Hotel. Families of employees were instructed to meet at the reunification site at Staybridge Suites Tampa East. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Citibank Center serves as the banking giant's regional data processing and communications hub, according to the developer's website. The campus is composed of four 130,000-square-foot three-story office buildings, and a 138,000-square-foot amenities building. The campus has roughly 25,000 employees and offers amenities such as dining services, a gym, child care facilities, a bank branch and shops including a drug store, dry cleaner, hairdresser and shoe repair shop. "The low-rise campus is surrounded by lushly landscaped berms with outdoor plazas, fountains, and waterfalls to provide a secluded, tranquil environment," the website states. "Each building is interconnected by enclosed walkways to ensure personnel comfort and building security as well as provide a homogenous atmosphere among the individual buildings and associated staff." articles.title: Helicopter crash near Miami leaves at least 1 dead, 2 injured: report
articles.summary: At least one person was killed and two others were seriously injured after a helicopter crashed near Nixon Beach off Key Biscayne, Florida. Investigators are examining the crash.
articles.body: A helicopter crashed in the waters off Miami on Wednesday, killing at least one person and seriously injuring two others, officials confirmed. The small helicopter went down near Nixon Beach, off Key Biscayne, Florida, shortly after 11 a.m., WSVN reported. The Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office said the crash occurred near Bill Baggs State Park. The U.S. Coast Guard confirmed that one of the three people aboard the helicopter died, while the other two were taken to a trauma center, according to The Associated Press. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue crews responded to the scene, where two people were rescued from the water, the report said. articles.title: Hasan Piker declares 'woke is back,' fantasizes about putting Donald Trump in prison
articles.summary: Hasan Piker's marathon 13-hour Twitch live stream drew over 200,000 viewers as he celebrated Democratic wins and declared "Trumpism is dying."
articles.body: Far-left streamer Hasan Piker took a victory lap on Tuesday, celebrating what he dubbed a "blue-clear apocalypse." Piker livestreamed on Twitch for more than 13 hours, offering real-time political commentary as Democrats took control of the House and Senate and won several key gubernatorial races. The stream, which at times drew more than 200,000 viewers, featured everything from Piker celebrating young voters who "duped" their parents into voting for socialists to calls for Republicans to land in prison. "Trumpism is dying, and I could not feel any better," Piker told his audience. At one point, he suggested, "Just imagine a world where Donald Trump is in f---ing prison." DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS "This is perhaps the worst possible scenario for the Republican Party, I think their odious agenda, their corruption, the destabilizing impact that they’ve had, the endless warfare and its consequences on the American economy are finally coming back to bite them," Piker added. "I think this might truly be the end of MAGA." The controversial streamer offered a steady stream of criticism aimed at conservatives, although it's sometimes unclear if he's exaggerating for effect or simply trolling his critics. As it became clear that Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) candidates and their allies were having a successful night, Piker expressed frustration that too many moderate Democrats were on ballots across the nation. "We should have been way more active, we should have f---ing ran socialists in every f---ing primary, dude. We should have been running socialists in every primary. I mean, look, I’m happy with what we’ve got result-wise, but we should have been running straight communists in some of these blue districts," Piker said. "And running the moderate-socialist wing of the DSA in these other ones." DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA BACKS 'OUR TWITCH STREAMER' HASAN PIKER, RIPS ANTI-SOCIALISM HOUSE RESOLUTION Throughout the night, Piker joked about throwing people in jail for misgendering, took celebratory shots of Japanese whiskey, repeatedly declared "woke is back," mocked conservatives who made him the "central figure of their midterm strategy" and repeated his claim that "Hamas is a thousand times better than Israel." "I stand by that statement because I believe in the accuracy of that statement," Piker said before suggesting many people share that sentiment. At one point, Piker said liberal pundits who cried on television when Trump was elected in 2024 have been "totally vindicated" by the midterm results. "I just want to put that out there, they’re cringe … but they’re totally vindicated," Piker said. "Look at what Donald Trump has done to, not just America, but to the rest of the world." INSIDE HASAN PIKER’S RADICAL VIEWS ON AMERICA, ISRAEL AND SOCIALISM Piker also joked that he was now the "Senate majority leader," taking credit for a variety of seats that flipped from Republican to Democratic control. "Since it’s now the Hasan Piker Democrats, as the Republicans said it was, it’s not my take, it’s their take. As the leader of the Democratic Party coalition, I’m officially branding woke back, we’re skipping Woke 2.0, we’re getting to Woke 3.0," Piker said. "Put your f---ing gender pronouns back in your LinkedIn profiles immediately," he added. "Or the Gaystapo will be knocking down your door." "American voters voted against racism," Piker said, arguing that Michigan Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed had faced a "barrage of Islamophobia" on the campaign trail. "It feels pretty good tonight to see that America rejected this kind of toxic politicking," Piker said. "America is ready for a new type of politics, one that centers the interest of the working class, and I will do everything in my power to ensure that we hold the Democratic Party to account to push forward with this agenda." ABDUL EL-SAYED REPORTEDLY CALLED HASAN PIKER WARNING HIS RHETORIC WAS 'COSTING' VOTES Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., appeared on Piker’s stream to dismiss Democrats who haven’t embraced the far-left streamer. "You would think, after this showing around the country, more people would say, ‘Yeah, you know what, we may not agree with him on everything but he’s got a huge following, he’s been clear, against the war in Iran, he’s been clear about the genocide in Gaza, the young people and people across the country are resonating with things that he’s saying about the war, yeah maybe we should engage," Khanna said. Piker also posted several messages on X that drew criticism. "WE'RE GONNA PUT YOUR ASS IN JAIL EVERYONE GET MORE WOKE RIGHT NOW," Piker posted as results poured in. When Texas state Rep. James Talarico defeated Republican Ken Paxton to win a U.S. Senate seat, delivering Democrats their first statewide victory in Texas in more than three decades, Piker declared, "GOD IS NONBINARY NOW MFS!!! ITS LAW!!!" CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Toward the end of the stream, Piker fantasized about putting Trump and Elon Musk in prison. "Dude, it would be so sweet to put him in jail," Piker said as a Trump interview played in the background. "Like, just think for a brief moment. How sweet would that be? I know the Democrats don’t have it in them but please, just close your eyes for a brief moment and just imagine a world where Donald Trump is in f---ing prison," he continued. "Elon is there, too, they have to hang out with one another as a part of the torturous conditions in this supermax facility that we put them in." Piker added, "A better future is possible." articles.title: Americans warned of violent protests as major tourist destination faces shutdown threat
articles.summary: A nationwide France strike on Nov. 5 threatens trains, public transportation and tourist attractions, the U.S. Embassy warned. Recent violent protests continue to be a concern.
articles.body: The U.S. Embassy has issued an urgent security alert for Americans in France, warning travelers to brace for severe disruptions, sudden curfews and the potential for violence as a massive nationwide strike threatens to paralyze the country on Thursday, Nov. 5. Beyond widespread shutdowns affecting public transit, schools and healthcare, authorities warn that recent demonstrations have already escalated into property destruction and looting. With France's four largest railway unions joining the multi-sector walkout, unapproved protests are expected to spill outside planned routes through the weekend. LOUVRE TURNS AWAY TOURISTS AS PARIS BRACES FOR RENEWED VIOLENCE FOLLOWING DESTRUCTIVE RIOTS In response, local officials are implementing strict, short-notice curfews that restrict free movement and block access to public landmarks in major areas, including Paris and its surrounding neighborhoods. The strike comes as unions demand higher wages, better working conditions and increased funding for public services, according to reports. Travelers could face disruptions to trains and other public transportation as demonstrations take place across the country. The embassy warned Americans to avoid protests and large gatherings, noting that recent demonstrations have turned violent and included property damage and looting. Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. Embassy for comment and further details. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER The latest warning comes after weeks of unrest created problems for travelers in Paris and other parts of France. Violent demonstrations in October prompted localized curfews in several cities, while riot police used tear gas near Place de la République in Paris as clashes unfolded, Fox News Digital previously reported. The unrest also affected some of the country's best-known tourist attractions. The Louvre was forced to close after protesters blocked entrances earlier in October, while travelers were advised to avoid common demonstration areas including Place de la République, Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation, Fox News Digital reported. French officials deployed thousands of law enforcement officers and redirected demonstrations away from central Paris after earlier unrest left thousands of businesses across France damaged or looted, Fox News Digital reported. With more demonstrations expected, the U.S. Embassy warned that protest routes could change and gatherings may take place outside areas approved by authorities. articles.title: 2 children and father fall to deaths in Pennsylvania in apparent murder-suicide
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania dad and his two children fell to their deaths on Election Day near a Mt. Lebanon parking garage in what police suspect was a murder-suicide.
articles.body: A Pennsylvania dad and his two children fell to their deaths on Election Day in what police suspect was a double murder-suicide. Their bodies were found a little after 4 p.m. Tuesday behind the Mt. Lebanon Municipal Building and near a neighboring parking garage, the Allegheny County Police Department said in a statement. “When first responders arrived on scene, they found an adult male and two children suffering injuries from an apparent fall,” police said. “First responders attempted life saving measures until medical professionals pronounced the three deceased on scene.” The dead were identified by the Allegheny County Medical Examiner’s Office as Patrick Lynch, 42; James Lynch, 8; and Caroline Lynch; 6. All three lived in Mt. Lebanon. “Preliminary information suggests that this incident is a murder-suicide and there is no danger to the community,” police said. Mt. Lebanon Police Chief Jason Haberman said at a press conference Tuesday “we’re treating this incident not as an accident.” “There will be a significant amount of trauma associated with this event for the community” he said. “Our condolences to everybody involved. ... Everyone in the Mt. Lebanon community will know someone involved in this incident.” Investigators have not divulged any details about what may have led to the deaths. articles.title: Fewer mothers to appear in court days after giving birth under new guidance
articles.summary: The changes follow concerns over the number of mothers summoned to safeguarding hearings shortly after labour.
articles.body:
The number of mothers going to court for child care proceedings within hours or days of giving birth will be reduced after new guidance was issued to judges.

The changes follow concerns about the increasing number of urgent applications brought to family courts for newborn babies where there is a safeguarding concern.

A recent BBC investigation highlighted the issue after hearing of the traumatic experience for mothers having to attend court while recovering from labour.

Under the new guidance issued by the Judiciary, same-day hearings should only be granted if a child's immediate safety is at risk to ensure intervention is "focused on cases that genuinely require it".

In October, the BBC reported the number of children involved in care proceedings before they reached their first birthdays was at a persistently high level across England, based on research from the universities of Lancaster and Oxford.

More than half of urgent care hearings in England in 2024-25 were for newborns, where mothers had to attend court within days of giving birth, or even potentially on the same day.

While there are cases where it is unsafe for parents to continue contact with their children, experts told the BBC's File on 4 Investigates that many babies may not have needed to go into care if support had been in place.

Since very young children who go into care are more likely to be adopted than older children, there are concerns from experts that some may have been permanently separated from their birth families unnecessarily.

Following a consultation, new guidance instructs courts to be rigorous in refusing to deal with cases that do not meet the criteria of urgency.

The expectation is that it would be extremely rare for an application to be made for a same-day hearing, the new guidance states.

It outlines that a same-day hearing should only be sought if a child's "immediate safety" would be compromised without the court's intervention.

Research from the Nuffield Family Justice Observatory found that over 70% of care proceedings involving babies in England were emergency hearings within two days of an application being made.

Emma Smale, its head of practice and policy, described the new guidance as a "welcome focus" on the issue.

She said the number of newborn babies in care proceedings in England and Wales subject to a same day hearing had doubled over a decade - from one in 10 in 2012-13 to one in five in 2022-23.

Smale said the process of separating a mother from their baby when they have just given birth is "widely accepted as deeply traumatic for all involved", and called into question the fairness of making "profoundly life-changing decisions" when a parent cannot effectively participate in the proceedings.

Under the new guidance, applicants for emergency or short notice listings - which take place within five days - will be required to justify with evidence why a case needs such a listing.

If a judge does not agree with the level of urgency, the case will be given a standard listing between days 12 and 18.

The Judiciary said the guidance is intended to help ensure parents and guardians "have time to respond more effectively to the application" and urgent judicial intervention is "focused on cases that genuinely require it".

A Newborn Baby Protocol has also been issued, which aims to provide a "greater level of fairness for child and parents" when care proceedings are issued immediately after the child's birth.

In England, early referral and assessment by local authority children's services will ensure the "timely provision" of preventative help, which should include identifying and strengthening family network resources, where this is in the child's best interests.

The protocol also states that before making any care order application, a Family Group Decision Making Meeting must be offered to parents, in line with the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026.

articles.title: London council to remove 700 dog waste bins in cost-cutting move; residents fear rise in dog fouling and 'poo Christmas trees'; owners told to use general litter bins or carry pets’ waste home
articles.summary: A London council's decision to remove 700 dedicated dog waste bins has raised concerns among residents, with fears that the move could lead to more dog
articles.body: A London council's decision to remove 700 dedicated dog waste bins has raised concerns among residents, with fears that the move could lead to more dog mess being dumped in public spaces. According to a report by The Telegraph, Hillingdon Council in west London plans to scrap all its dedicated dog waste bins as part of a cost-cutting exercise, asking pet owners to use ordinary litter bins or carry their dogs' waste home.The Telegraph's report from Ruislip Lido highlighted an unusual problem, with discarded dog waste bags occasionally being tied to tree branches, creating what locals have described as 'dog poo Christmas trees'. The woodland surrounding the reservoir already features festive decorations, including reindeer and snowmen, but the waste-filled bags have become an unwelcome sight.Why Hillingdon Council is removing 700 dog waste binsThe council's decision is part of a wider effort to reduce spending. The removal of the 700 dedicated bins is expected to generate annual savings of around £160,000, of which £60,000 will be reinvested in street cleaning. This would leave the authority with a net saving of approximately £100,000 annually.The scale of the waste involved is considerable. Around 14.5 tonnes of dog waste are collected across the borough every month, amounting to approximately 174 tonnes annually.Under the new arrangements, dog owners will be encouraged to dispose of bagged waste in the borough's nearly 1,500 ordinary public litter bins or take it home for disposal.Residents fear more dog fouling in public spacesThe decision has prompted concerns among residents and dog owners, particularly over whether ordinary litter bins can handle the additional waste.The Ruislip Residents' Association has questioned the council's decision, pointing out that some existing dog waste bins already overflow and that several locations do not have ordinary litter bins nearby.There are also concerns about unpleasant smells, overflowing bins and foxes scattering waste bags, as general litter bins may not offer the same facilities as dedicated dog waste bins.The Telegraph's report also highlighted the possibility of more waste bags being left hanging from trees and bushes if dog owners cannot find suitable disposal points.Council's plans for the transitionHillingdon Council maintains that ordinary litter bins can accommodate bagged dog waste and that using existing infrastructure will simplify waste collection.The authority plans to remove the dedicated bins in phases and introduce stickers and temporary signs informing residents that ordinary litter bins can also accept dog waste.Council officials believe the changes will eliminate the need to operate two separate waste collection services while maintaining disposal facilities for dog owners.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Indiana dentist whose company bought him a $130,000 Cybertruck fought a child support order of $964 a week; an appeals court upheld parts of his income calculation but ordered a fresh look at the vehicle benefit
articles.summary: An Indiana dentist who challenged a child support order of $964 a week has won a partial victory before the Indiana Court of Appeals.
articles.body: An Indiana dentist who challenged a child support order of $964 a week has won a partial victory before the Indiana Court of Appeals. Christopher Chisler, a dentist and owner of several dental practices, argued that the trial court overstated his income by counting distributions from his businesses and by treating a $130,000 Tesla Cybertruck purchased by one of his companies as a personal benefit. The appeals court agreed with him on the vehicle issue, but it upheld much of the lower court’s approach to his income and support calculation. The case, Christopher T. Chisler v. Krysta Chisler, arose after Chisler and Krysta Chisler divorced in 2022. Their marriage produced one child, and the dispute later focused on whether Chisler’s business income, company-purchased vehicles and other financial arrangements should count toward his child support obligation. The Indiana Court of Appeals affirmed parts of the support order, reversed others and sent the case back for further proceedings, as reported by Justia U.S. Law and The Indiana Lawyer. Read more about it here:The dispute over incomeChisler owns or has interests in several dental businesses, including Greenwood Modern Dentistry, Fishers Modern Dentistry, Midwest Dental Partners and C&C Holdings LLC. The trial court calculated his weekly income at $5,950, a figure that included distributions from his businesses and the value of company-provided vehicles.On appeal, Chisler challenged several elements of that calculation. He argued that the court wrongly treated distributions from his businesses as income, improperly denied certain deductions, and wrongly included the Cybertruck as part of his available resources, as per the reports. He also disputed the court’s handling of health insurance premiums, arrears, educational expenses and attorney fees.The appeals court found sufficient grounds to include business distributions in his income calculation. It also rejected some of the deductions Chisler sought, while affirming the overall structure and amount of the child support order. But the court did not accept every part of the trial court’s reasoning, particularly on the Cybertruck.The $130,000 Cybertruck issueOne of the most unusual questions in the case involved a Tesla Cybertruck purchased by Fishers Modern Dentistry for $130,000. The trial court included the value of that vehicle in Chisler’s income for child support purposes, treating it as a benefit provided by his company.The Court of Appeals reversed that part of the ruling. It found that the trial court had not adequately explained why the Cybertruck should be counted as income or as a personal benefit to Chisler. The court remanded the issue for a fresh assessment of whether the vehicle actually provided Chisler with a measurable economic benefit that should be included in his child support calculation.This matters because business purchases can serve different purposes. A company vehicle may be a legitimate business expense, a personal perk, or something in between. The appeals court did not say the Cybertruck could never count toward Chisler’s income. It said the trial court needed to explain and support that conclusion more clearly before including it.What the court upheldThe appeals court affirmed the trial court’s decision to include distributions from Chisler’s businesses in his income. That finding is significant because it means a parent cannot necessarily avoid child support obligations by keeping compensation in a company rather than taking it as salary.The court also denied some of the deductions Chisler wanted, while affirming the overall structure and amount of the child support order. In practical terms, the weekly support amount of $964 was not overturned. The case will instead return to the trial court to revisit specific calculations, including the vehicle benefit, the health insurance credit, capital expenditure deductions and educational contributions.The court also addressed Chisler’s challenge to the arrears payment schedule. The appeals court found sufficient grounds to support the trial court’s approach to his ability to pay arrears, while remanding for adjustments connected to the other recalculations.Why the case mattersThe decision shows how child support cases can become complicated when a parent owns a business. Income is not always a simple salary figure. It can include distributions, company benefits, retained earnings and other financial arrangements that may affect a parent’s real ability to pay.The Cybertruck issue also illustrates the need for courts to distinguish between business expenses and personal benefits. A vehicle bought by a company may be used for work, but it may also provide a parent with personal transportation, status or savings that would otherwise come out of personal income. The appeals court’s remand requires the trial court to make that distinction with evidence and reasoning.For parents in similar disputes, the ruling offers two lessons. First, courts may look beyond a salary figure when calculating support. Second, a parent challenging an income calculation must show why a particular benefit or deduction should be treated differently, rather than simply arguing that the number is too high.A partial win, not a full reversalChisler did not persuade the appeals court to throw out the child support order. The court affirmed much of the trial court’s calculation and left the overall support framework intact. But he did succeed in forcing a closer look at the Cybertruck and several other financial questions.The case now returns to the Hancock Circuit Court for further proceedings. The trial court must reconsider the vehicle benefit, health insurance credit, capital expenditure deductions and educational contributions, while applying the appeals court’s guidance on business distributions and arrears.The outcome is a reminder that child support law often turns on detailed financial evidence. In this case, the difference between a company expense and a personal benefit could affect how much a father pays each week. The Indiana Court of Appeals has now made clear that such questions deserve a careful, well-supported answer.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Govt opens absorption path for all Agniveers, Rajnath says 'move aimed at creating younger, fitter, future-ready military'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In a big overhaul of the Agnipath scheme, Modi govt Wednesday extended the service of Agniveers from four years to six, with increased
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In a big overhaul of the Agnipath scheme, Modi govt Wednesday extended the service of Agniveers from four years to six, with increased remuneration, and opened the path for their absorption as regular soldiers. The Union Cabinet’s decision will clear the way for three lakh Agniveers, including the first batch of 18,300 who will complete their four-year tenure by Dec 31 this year.Calling the two-year extension the ‘second tour of duty’ for Agniveers, defence minister Rajnath Singh said, “ This would provide enrollment of all willing Agniveers as regular soldiers after the tenure of 4/6 years, who meet the selection criteria. This decision is continuation of long-term structural reforms of our defence forces, aimed at creating a younger, fitter, technologically equipped and future-ready military. It is not merely a recruitment policy; it is a way forward to prepare India’s military for the changing character of warfare.”The changes will help remove heartburn in various recruitment zones. The decision is also politically significant as the opposition has time and again questioned the aim of launching a short-tenure recruitment scheme.Chief of Defence Staff Gen N S Raja Subramani said, “When the Agnipath scheme was rolled out, we emphasised it was not cast in stone. We said we would evaluate the performances of the Agniveers and conduct continuous reviews.”Calling it a “very significant day for defence forces and our Agniveers”, Gen Subramani, at a media briefing with I&B minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, said as envisaged earlier, 25% of Agniveers will be offered regular employment based on merit during the first four years.“For the remaining 75% Agniveers, another engagement period of two years has been approved by Cabinet. Thereafter, all Agniveers will be offered enrolment as regular soldiers subject to their willingness and meeting objective selection criteria comprising parameters of physical fitness, vigilance clearance and clean discipline record,” he said.“While the Navy batch was going to complete the tenure on Nov 21, the IAF batch between Dec 21 and 25, and Army batch on Dec 31,” a defence official told TOI.Gen Subramani said, “During the two-year engagement period, 75% Agniveers will get increased remuneration as compared to the earlier four-year period. During the fifth year, they will get Rs 43,500 salary per month and during the sixth year, Rs 47,500.”The changes in the scheme were brought in before the first batch of 18,300 Agniveers were to exit the armed forces after completing their four-year tenure. “While the Navy batch was going to complete the tenure on Nov 21, the IAF batch between Dec 21 and 25, and Army batch on Dec 31,” a defence source told TOI.The short-tenure Agnipath scheme was rolled out in June 2022 during the Covid period amid realisation that the ballooning salary and pension bill left little for modernisation and augmentation of weaponry. It was also influenced by the realisation that the changed nature of warfare, with technology playing a bigger role, may have reduced the cruciality of the number of boots on the ground.The increased allocation for defence in recent years and revenue from defence exports increased the elbow room for govt to accommodate Agniveers.“Those Agniveers who are not willing to continue in the services after the four-year period will receive a Seva Nidhi package (comprising their own 30% monthly contribution plus the matching contribution from govt and accrued interest),” Gen Subramani said.“The military is happy with the overall performance of Agniveer recruits, who are also deployed in forward areas,” he said, adding women Agniveers are also doing good. “Some of them even deployed on aircraft carriers INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya,” he informed.The CDS also made it clear that there will be no problem of cohesion of different Agniveer batches into the regular Army. He said the military had been considering the proposal for quite some months before the Cabinet took the decision.

articles.title: Democratic progressive wing notches win in California Central Valley
articles.summary: Campaign focused on cost of living issues and backlash over ICE raids pays dividends for progressive Randy Villegas.
articles.body:
Democratic candidate Randy Villegas has defeated Republican incumbent David Valadao in the race for California’s 22nd congressional district, clinching one of the state’s most closely watched congressional races and notching another win for the Democratic Party’s progressive left.

Villegas, an educator who grew up in the Central Valley as the son of Mexican immigrants, ousted the Republican representative after a campaign that won support from figures such as Senator Bernie Sanders and railed against the rising cost of living, healthcare cuts, and sweeping immigration raids .

“I want to take a moment to acknowledge my family. Both of my parents, who I’m blessed to have with me here today. I’ve gotta tell you, the reason I believe in this country, the reason I believe in the United States, is because of the sacrifices that they made,” Villegas said in remarks to his supporters gathered in the city of Bakersfield on Tuesday evening, calling the result a “historic victory for the Central Valley”.

“And let me tell you, that victory is not because of me. It is because of us,” he added.

Here are some of the key takeaways from the race.

The story of the district fits a larger one playing out across the country as votes come in on election night: angry about surging prices that were driven partly by the Trump administration’s decision to launch a war on Iran, and overreach in areas such as ICE raids, voters decided to punish the president and his party.

Polls had indicated for months that the president had become deeply unpopular, and that this trend was closely linked to collapsing faith in his handling of the economy and cost of living, issues that had previously helped return him to the White House in 2024.

Despite his image as a relative moderate with strong ties to the Central Valley, Valadao did not escape that trend on Tuesday night.

Immigration raids trigger backlash among Latino voters

Following Trump’s win in 2024, much was made of the Republican Party’s successful inroads with Latino voters despite the party’s embrace of rhetoric vilifying immigrants and restrictive immigration policies.

Less than two years later, those promising gains have entirely evaporated.

Incensed over the administration’s aggressive and often indiscriminate approach to immigration enforcement and the toll of rising prices, Latino voters across the country swung heavily back towards the Democrats.

“We have people who said that they regret having voted for him [Trump], because he has not done what he promised,” a member of the United Farm Workers (UFW) labour union who knocked doors in Latino communities for Villegas, told Al Jazeera on Monday.

Residents and officials in the Central Valley said that ICE raids sent shockwaves through immigrant and Latino communities, with arrests of farmworkers and family members cutting against the administration’s claims that it was targeting criminals.

Villegas slammed the raids and linked them to Valadao’s support for a massive increase in the budget for ICE, one of the agencies at the centre of the mass deportation raids.

A recent survey from the Pew Research Center found that 56 percent of US voters now view ICE unfavourably, making it one of the least popular agencies in the federal government.

Progressives make the case for their competitiveness

Before facing off against Valadao on Tuesday night, Villegas had to win a hard-fought primary race against California State Assembly member Jasmeet Bains, a candidate aligned with the party’s establishment wing who warned that his progressive positions would be too far to the left in the traditionally conservative region.

But Villegas and his supporters challenged that premise. His populist message seems to have resonated in a race dominated by concerns about the cost of living and access to healthcare, and at a time when many feel that politics and the economy are skewed in favour of the wealthy and well-connected.

Villegas won endorsements from Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and energised supporters from the party’s base, including members of organised labour who pounded the pavement to get out the vote.

“We beat the Democratic establishment. We beat the Republican establishment. We beat corporate PAC money. We beat AIPAC!” Villegas told supporters on Tuesday night.

Villegas can now add his name to the list of elected officials seeking to prove that progressives can win tough races outside of traditional strongholds.

“Randy’s race has shown us that the Central Valley cannot be counted out of following the really urgent change that we need in every corner of our country,” said Manpreet Kaur, the progressive vice mayor of Bakersfield who was an early supporter of Villegas. “And the Central Valley is included in that.”

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Cabinet is learnt to have approved another extension for the Commission of Inquiry into the Manipur violence, giving it another year, until May 20, 2027, to submit its report. This is the sixth extension granted to it since the commission was constituted in Sept 2023.As per the original notification issued in Sept 2023, the commission was required to submit its report by Nov 2023. Its mandate included inquiring into the causes and spread of violence and riots targeting members of different communities in Manipur on May 3, 2023, and thereafter.The commission was also tasked with examining whether there were any lapses or dereliction of duty by the authorities concerned or individuals, and whether the administrative measures taken to prevent and deal with the violence were adequate. It was also asked to examine the sequence of events leading to the violence and other related matters.The ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur on May 3, 2023, has since claimed more than 300 lives and displaced thousands of people, besides deepening divisions between the state’s Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities.The latest extension means the commission will now get nearly four years to complete an inquiry that was originally expected to conclude within months.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Man allegedly held teen captive in basement, forced her to remove braces with pliers after Snapchat meeting
articles.summary: Kylie Arellano was allegedly forced to remove her braces with pliers and confined to a basement for over 500 days before her rescue in Oregon.
articles.body: The missing Utah teenager found alive in Oregon nearly 18 months after her disappearance was allegedly beaten repeatedly and forced to remove her braces with pliers to hide her identity, according to disturbing new details in the case. Kylie Arellano, now 17, vanished from Garden City, Utah, on May 29, 2025, when she was 15. Federal authorities have now charged a 39-year-old man in her alleged captivity. In court documents reviewed by Fox News Digital, Adam Hunter Harmel allegedly became "very violent and aggressive, often hitting" the teen and further forced her to remove her braces with pliers so that she could not be identified. MISSING UTAH TEEN KYLIE ARELLANO FOUND SAFE IN OREGON AFTER 500-DAY SEARCH The federal complaint also paints a chilling picture of captivity inside Harmel's home, where Harmel allegedly confined the teenager to the basement, where the two shared a bed. To prevent her from escaping, the complaint says, Harmel also "kept a knife under his pillow and made MV [minor victim] sleep against the wall." Investigators said Harmel had expressed a desire to start a family with the teenager, stated that he was interested in minors and repeatedly sexually assaulted her in 2025 and 2026, according to the complaint. Harmel allegedly transported Arellano across state lines with the intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. 12-YEAR-OLD NORTH CAROLINA GIRL ESCAPES ALLEGED KIDNAPPER AFTER BEING FORCED INTO TRUCK The criminal complaint, filed Nov. 2 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah, also outlines a timeline of alleged grooming, isolation and abuse. For more than 500 days, Arellano's mother held out hope after finding her daughter's jacket discarded in the driveway and her phone turned off. That wait ended Nov. 1, when law enforcement rescued the teenager from a home in Oregon following a tip from the parent of another player of the online game "Among Us." According to an affidavit written by FBI Special Agent Andrea Elder, Arellano's family first reported in 2025 that she had been groomed online, with communications beginning on gaming platforms before moving to other social media apps. According to a law enforcement source, the suspect allegedly met the teenager on Snapchat before her disappearance. During the investigation, the FBI also learned that Arellano was allegedly groomed on platforms that are often used by Nihilistic Violent Extremist (NVE) Groups members to solicit sexually explicit photos and maiming photos, according to a release issued by the Department of Justice (DOJ). JILLIAN MICHAELS URGES PARENTS TO FIGHT BACK AGAINST BIG TECH'S 'ADDICTIVE' GRIP ON KIDS Authorities allege that, in May 2025, Harmel met the teenager online, claimed he had a disability involving his "messed up" hips and offered her money to travel to Oregon. Harmel drove from Oregon to Perry, Utah, to pick her up on or about May 29, 2025. Immediately after she entered the vehicle, according to the complaint, Harmel threw her phone into a river in Logan Canyon, drove her to his home in Huntington, Oregon, and told her she was not allowed to leave. A housemate living at the home told the FBI that Harmel claimed he had brought home a "new girlfriend" from Utah. The housemate did not see the teenager until about two months after her arrival, when she ran back into the basement. According to the complaint, Harmel provided Arellano with a phone that lacked cellular data capabilities, limiting her internet access to Wi-Fi. Her path to freedom began in mid-October 2026, when she connected with another minor while playing "Among Us." After moving their conversation to another social media app, Arellano revealed her real identity and told the minor she was being held against her will at a man's home in Oregon. She also said she thought police were no longer looking for her. FRANCE BECOMES FIRST EU NATION TO BAN SOCIAL MEDIA FOR CHILDREN UNDER 15 Her mother contacted the FBI, which monitored a Nov. 1 video call with Arellano during which she showed investigators the knife Harmel kept and other evidence corroborating her claims. That same day, Oregon State Police and federal agents rescued the teenager and took her for medical treatment. A search of Harmel's residence uncovered knives, BB guns and sexual lubricant, according to the complaint. Harmel was arrested during a traffic stop in Ontario, Oregon. Harmel was scheduled to make his initial appearance in federal court Wednesday. In a statement, U.S. Attorney for the District of Utah Melissa Holyoak said the priority in the case was the "safe return of the minor victim." "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP FBI Director Kash Patel issued a similar warning to those who target and exploit children. "The FBI and our partners are coming for you. We are using every tool at our disposal to combat nihilistic violent extremism, bring offenders to justice, and protect America’s most vulnerable," he said.

articles.title: She once cooked meals for 500 homeless people from her Atlanta apartment; now entrepreneur Jasmine Crowe's company has served 30 million meals and rescued food from landfills
articles.summary: Before she became the founder of a growing food recovery business, Jasmine Crowe was spending hours in grocery stores, cooking in her Atlanta apartment
articles.body: Before she became the founder of a growing food recovery business, Jasmine Crowe was spending hours in grocery stores, cooking in her Atlanta apartment and loading meals into her car for people who had nowhere else to turn. What began as a personal effort to feed hundreds of people gradually exposed a problem she had not initially set out to solve: businesses were throwing away perfectly edible food while families and homeless communities struggled to find enough to eat. As reported by Forbes, in 2017, Crowe turned that observation into Goodr, a technology-driven company that connects surplus food with people who need it. Its reported reach has since grown to millions of meals.Jasmine Crowe's Atlanta apartment became the starting point for Sunday SoulLong before Goodr became a business, Crowe was organising meals for people experiencing homelessness in Atlanta. Her initiative, called Sunday Soul, grew out of her desire to provide restaurant-quality dining experiences to people who rarely had access to them. Rather than simply handing out food, she wanted guests to sit down, enjoy a proper meal and be treated with dignity.The work was considerably more demanding than arranging a weekly dinner. Crowe would spend as many as 40 hours across three or four days shopping for ingredients, comparing prices, collecting coupons and preparing food. She sometimes cooked for as many as 500 people, working from her own kitchen before transporting the meals to locations around the city. The gatherings eventually extended beyond Atlanta, reaching communities in Washington DC and New Orleans.For several years, she continued organising these dinners largely through her own resources. The effort attracted attention after footage of one of her pop-up dining events circulated widely online. People watching the video were interested in how the meals had been arranged and, in particular, which restaurants or grocery stores had supplied the food.How Jasmine Crowe turned America's food waste problem into Goodr in 2017Crowe began examining how restaurants, supermarkets and large organisations handled food they could no longer sell or serve. articles.title: In Florida, 150 tons of old concrete pipes, junction boxes and steel were headed for landfill; crews cleaned the material and lowered it 70 feet into the Gulf to create a new artificial reef for marine life
articles.summary: What was once considered industrial waste is now set to become an underwater habitat for marine life off Florida's coast.
articles.body: What was once considered industrial waste is now set to become an underwater habitat for marine life off Florida's coast. Crews have repurposed approximately 150 tons of discarded concrete and steel, including old pipes and junction boxes, and deployed the material on the Gulf seabed near Panama City Beach to create a new artificial reef. The project, carried out in March 2026, is part of the region's ongoing efforts to expand marine habitats while finding productive uses for materials that would otherwise be discarded. According to local broadcaster WJHG/WECP, the structures were lowered around 70 feet underwater at a permitted site southwest of St. Andrews Pass. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) and the University of Florida's IFAS Extension have also documented the wider artificial reef programme and its ecological benefits. Scroll down to read more.From discarded construction material to underwater habitatThe materials used in the project were originally destined for a landfill. They included concrete pipes, junction boxes and other industrial components that were no longer needed for their original purpose. Instead of sending them to waste facilities, the project team decided to give them a second life beneath the water.Before deployment, the material was cleaned and prepared to ensure it met environmental requirements for use as an artificial reef. The structures were then transported offshore and lowered onto the seabed at a permitted location approximately 6.08 nautical miles southwest of St. Andrews Pass.The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's deployment records identify the March 19 installation as RESTORE Rubble 9 and 10. Its records list 159 tons of secondary-use concrete at a depth of approximately 72 feet, providing a more precise figure for the deployment.How artificial reefs help marine lifeArtificial reefs are designed to provide underwater structures in areas where natural hard-bottom habitats may be limited. Once established, they offer surfaces where algae, sponges, corals and other marine organisms can attach and grow. These organisms gradually help create a food-rich environment, attracting smaller fish and invertebrates. Larger species can then use the structures for shelter, feeding and breeding.According to the University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences, secondary-use concrete pipes and culverts can be arranged to create different spaces and openings, increasing habitat complexity for marine animals. Over time, these structures can support a wider range of marine life, from small crustaceans to larger fish. The new installation is expected to follow a similar process. Project organisers anticipate that marine organisms will begin colonising the material within the first year, gradually establishing a functioning underwater habitat.A boost for fishing and divingThe project is also expected to benefit people who visit Panama City Beach for recreational activities. Artificial reefs attract fish and create additional locations for anglers, while divers can explore the developing underwater structures. Florida already has an extensive artificial reef network. The FWC reports that thousands of artificial reefs have been established in state and federal waters, providing habitat for marine species while supporting recreational fishing, diving and coastal economies.Concrete and steel are among the commonly used materials because they can provide durable structures when properly prepared, positioned and secured. Their deployment is subject to environmental and permitting requirements to ensure they are suitable for long-term use underwater.For Erin Graham, the artificial reef coordinator and coastal resource manager involved in the Panama City Beach programme, the work also has a personal connection. Having grown up fishing and diving, she sees the project as a way to create more opportunities for marine life as well as for people who enjoy spending time on the water. The latest deployment adds to Panama City Beach's expanding artificial reef programme, demonstrating how discarded industrial materials can be repurposed into structures that support marine habitats and provide new recreational opportunities.You use AI every day. articles.title: South Wales Metro £200m tram-trains sit barely used for three years
articles.summary: The final piece in a £2bn rail project is late, with less than half of the trains tested.
articles.body:
A new fleet of publicly funded trains that cost more than £200m still remain mostly unused more than three years after the first one was delivered.

They were initially promised to be fully up and running by 2022 but Transport for Wales' boss has said it might not be until the end of 2027 when their tram-trains will be in full service.

Data obtained by the BBC reveals that less than half of the 36 fleet - what TfW call the "final piece" in their £2bn South Wales Metro project - have passed rigorous statutory testing.

TfW chief executive James Price said he wants trains that work "100% well, 100% of the time" before putting them into full service.

TfW's flagship scheme to transform an old Victorian railway into a turn-up-and-go rapid transit service, similar to the London Underground and Manchester Metrolink, is Wales' single-biggest infrastructure project since devolution in 1999.

It has been hit by delays and rising costs and the Welsh government-owned rail operator has missed numerous self-imposed targets to bring the tram-trains into full service across the south Wales valleys.

Officially known as Class 398 Citylink multiple units, they were ordered from Swiss manufacturer Stadler in 2018 and the first arrived in Wales in March 2023.

The King and former Prime Minister Keir Starmer have been on one but barely any passengers have.

Six tram-trains, worth about £8m each which can run both on urban streets and rail, are currently in passenger testing across the valleys network.

But they have been temporarily removed from service on occasions for what TfW described as "teething issues" and "early reliability challenges" because of "software" problems.

Commuters have now been told they will not be fully in service across the whole 105-mile (170km) network until 2027 - five years later than originally promised.

"It's definitely frustrating," said TfW boss Price.

"Everyone would want something to work first time, wouldn't they? It's frustrating but not unexpected."

Passengers have been told the doubling of services from two to four trains an hour will begin between Cardiff and Aberdare, Merthyr Tydfil and Treherbert by the end of 2027 - a pledge passengers were also initially told would happen by 2022 .

Commuters on those routes have had new trains since 2024 when TfW introduced their class 756 units onto the old valley line after years of delays and complaints about old rolling stock .

"They got delivered earlier and the reliability was better," said Price.

"That meant that we weren't able to test the trams against the original date. The key thing for me was getting new trains into service and maximising value for money."

Sixteen of TfW's 36 tram-train fleet have passed testing to ensure the three-carriage units are safe to run on the UK rail network - with 20 yet to complete the scrutiny required by the rail regulator.

Those tests on some of the vehicles started in 2024 - and data obtained by the BBC via a Freedom of Information request shows they can take anything between six weeks and two years.

"Trains are not a mass-produced vehicle and you only experience problems when you bring them into service," said Price.

"I don't accept there is a problem with the tram-trains but the biggest issue is a software issue. That's because the whole fleet is controlled by one big software package and we've tried to automate as much of the train as we can.

"The good thing when automation is fully working, any improvements we make with the trains can be delivered through software rather than hard engineering.

"That will be cheaper, quicker and more reliable because if you do it on one train, all the other trains will behave in the same way."

TfW said they didn't launch the tram-trains with a "big fanfare" and opted for a customer testing approach as they feared they "might come out of service".

"What we want is trains that work 100% of the time, 100% well," said Price.

"We've been achieving 95% on-time reliability on the valleys network and that's the high standard we want to achieve before bringing something into passenger service in large numbers."

Price said he met Stadler's chief executive recently in Germany for talks in a bid to speed up the tram-train rollout.

Stadler has said it is "working closely" with TfW to address "minor issues" in what they have described "one of the UK's most advanced battery tram-trains".

"Testing and validation activities have progressed in phases, resulting in the identification and implementation of normal refinements, including software updates, as part of the fleet introduction process," a spokesperson said.

TfW said part of the delay is because the line electrification infrastructure was only finished in March because of hold ups caused by Covid and supply chain impact caused by the Ukraine war.

But one railway expert reckons the tram-trains are maybe just too complicated.

"It's a pretty ambitious project," said rail engineer and broadcaster Gareth Dennis.

"The challenge of having such complicated trains trying to do everything to reduce the cost of the infrastructure requires a lot of stuff to be working on the train. All of that has to be tested to make sure it always works."

The line infrastructure will tell the trains what to do through a series of beacons and TfW claim the South Wales Metro will be one of the most technologically advanced railway networks when the tram-trains are in full service.

While 100% of the network is fully electrified, only two-thirds has traditional overhead electric wires.

By not electrifying the entire track and using on-board batteries for non-electrified sections, TfW say they've saved about £400m and years of time.

But Dennis fears the tram-trains are "being delivered as part of cutting some corners" like not doing complete overhead wire electrification" as he believes TfW try to get new services delivered quickly.

"It is the case that this is the first deployment that has pulled all this stuff together - being a tram, a train, having a battery and discontinuous electrification," added the host of the #railnatter podcast.

"But that isn't necessarily a very good idea and that's why it's not common."

But TfW have said that technology already works on the bigger 756 trains, the temporary stop-gap before the nippier, purpose-built vehicles are rolled out.

Opposition politicians in Wales have questioned why most of the tram-trains are "just sitting in a depot gathering dust".

"Taxpayers deserve to know what has gone wrong, how delays have turned into years and the costs are spiralling out of control," said Reform's shadow transport minister Jason O'Connell.

TfW, who took over the running of the £5bn Wales and Borders franchise during Covid, say their south Wales valleys upgrades have been "quick".

" If you think we didn't get hold of the lines until 2021 and by 2025 most of the work was substantially complete," said Price.

"And today we basically have 100% new trains - it's not as quick as we originally said but compared to any other project in the UK, it's very quick."

TfW have said introducing the tram-trains fully into service and operating four trains an hour on the three lines between Cardiff and Aberdare, Merthyr Tydfil and Treherbert is the "final piece of the South Wales Metro jigsaw".

"The reason for, I guess, the relatively slow pace is that we need to train quite a few hundred crew then do signalling work at Queen Street station in Cardiff," said Price.

"I do fully expect to see four trains an hour by the end of next year definitely."

The Welsh government said TfW had already delivered "transformative improvements on the valleys network" and new trains would eventually "unlock turn-up-and-go" services across the valleys and Cardiff.

"Whilst some issues have delayed the introduction of the new tram trains TfW remains on target to complete the full rollout by the end of next year," it added.
